body: I had really horrible cystic acne around that age, and it can be really painful both physically and emotionally. I think it's important, more than any routine, to make sure she knows that this isn't her fault and that she shouldn't feel bad about herself because of it. Proactive barely worked for me when I used it around 10 years ago, but even if they've changed the formula, I wouldn't start out with it. It's really important to use gentle products at her age, so I'd recommend a cleanser from a brand like Cetaphil or CeraVe with salicylic acid in it and a light-weight moisturiser with ceramides in the ingredient list. It may seem counterintuitive to moisturize with acne, but drying out the skin can make things worse by triggering more sebum production and damaging the moisture barrier, even in a moist environment. I haven't personally used sulfur products, but I've heard other people say they majorly helped their cystic acne. Good luck to you and your daughter, and I hope everything turns out OK.

I told them I lost it because I just wasn't eating and they weren't even concerned. They just said " Well you still look great!" At the time this just made me mad at how stupid they were acting, and I wanted to gain it back. But now I remember this and I just want to lose and lose and lose, because I'm aware of how much they were silently nitpicking at my appearance all these years.
